title: Pinning cost playbook for SMB customers
summary: Working playbook to evaluate, price, and operate region pinning for small-medium customers. Focuses on cost transparency, reduced-risk migration patterns, operator steps for temporary exemptions, and telemetry needed to gate rollouts.
body:
Purpose:
This is an internal working playbook intended to help sales-eng, solutions, and ops evaluate region pin requests from SMB customers and make fast, repeatable decisions that balance compliance with cost/operational burden.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated customers requesting region pinning or partial residency guarantees.
- Prioritizes SMB customers (monthly spend typically <$25k) but includes guidance that scales up to mid-market.
- Covers: pricing heuristics, short-term exemption paths, operator runbook for pin creation and rollback, migration patterns, and telemetry metrics to monitor.

Assumptions and constraints (quick):
- SMB customers more price-sensitive; many will accept partial residency guarantees (metadata/localization) vs full-data anchoring.
- Dedicated capacity requests for SMBs are rare; instead we expect a mix of region pin + soft-affinity + replicated anchors.
- Legal team defines when a hard pin is required; this doc handles operational cost/telemetry side.

Core pricing heuristics (for initial quote):
1) Baseline: hosted (no pin) = list price.
2) Soft-pin (preferred for SMB): +10-20% uplift depending on region and expected token volume; assumes no reserved capacity.
3) Hard-pin / anchored storage: add fixed monthly surcharge to cover cross-region replication and storage escrow (typical range $2k-$8k depending on data size and retention).
4) SLA/priority routing: optional addons for guaranteed capacity (reserved bursts) priced separately per request.

Why these numbers? (short rationale)
- Soft-pin adds routing complexity and higher cold-cache miss rates; we model 10-20% additional token cost from increased latency-sensitive re-compute.
- Hard-pin incurs storage replication/escrow and operational overhead for evidence packaging and audit logs.
- For SMBs the fixed surcharge must be kept simple and small; if expected monthly token spend exceeds X (TBD) switch to dedicated pricing.

Customer experience tiers (recommended):
- Tier A (Least friction): Soft-pin + transparency report; no contractual anchoring. Use for customers asking for region preference or low-risk regulatory needs.
- Tier B: Soft-pin + daily residency evidence bundle + 30-day retention for anchor logs. For customers that want some auditability for compliance attestations.
- Tier C (High assurance for a fee): Hard-pin with committed anchor storage and SLA-backed guarantees. Best for enterprise but can be offered to SMBs at clear price point.

Operator runbook (quick steps for creating a temporary exemption/pin):
1) Intake: Solutions Eng creates a ticket with required legal justification and customer region(s). Attach product template (link: CONFLUENCE-1234).
2) Risk check: Oncall SRE runs residency-check script (JIRA-OPS-987) to show current tenant placement and expected cross-region latency impact.
3) Estimate cost delta: Use pricing heuristic table (attached) and produce a 30/90/365 day cost projection.
4) Create soft-pin: Apply region preference flag in tenant metadata. Do not alter storage anchors. Notify customer of eventual fallback behavior.
5) Monitor telemetry for 72 hours (see telemetry section). If errors/evictions spike -> escalate to infra-runbook.
6) Move to hard-pin only after legal sign-off and finance confirms surcharge acceptance.

Telemetry and gating signals (what we need to measure):
- Token cost delta per tenant (rolling 7d and 30d).
- Cache miss rate for pinned tenants vs baseline.
- Request latency P50/P95/P99 before and after pin.
- Cross-region egress bytes and number of anchor writes.
- Evidence bundle generation success rate and packaging lag.
- Operator actions taken and time-to-rollforward/rollback.

Migration patterns for SMBs (practical playbooks):
- Phase 0 (Assessment): Light audit of data residency needs, recommended tier, and estimated cost.
- Phase 1 (Soft-pin trial): 14–30 day trial soft-pin; surface telemetry and SLA impact. Present evidence to customer.
- Phase 2 (Optional hard-pin pilot): Small scope hard-pin for a subset of users/data; validate anchor packaging and audit flow.
- Phase 3 (Roll): If satisfied, move to full hard-pin and invoice surcharge starting first full billing cycle.

Customer comm (template snippets):
- "We can provision a region preference (soft-pin) within 48 hours. This balances reduced cross-border transfer with lower cost than a full anchor. We will monitor for any performance impact and share a residency report after 14 days."
- "For strict legal requirements we offer a paid anchor package which includes packaged audit evidence and an SLA for region fidelity."

Edge cases and open questions (TODOs):
- How do we price multi-region anchors for customers with multi-jurisdiction requirements? (ACTION: finance to propose formula).
- Clarify definition of SMB in pricing docs (spend bands vary by region).
- Behavior when customer requests pin removal mid-cycle (pro-rate or full-month charge?).
- Automating the evidence bundle for Tier B (reduce operator work).

Minimum telemetry dashboard (MVP):
- Single view per pinned tenant showing: current pin state, latency delta, token cost delta, cache miss rate, last evidence bundle timestamp, and active alerts.

Operator quick-check checklist (for oncall):
- Verify ticket has legal justification and signed PDF (if Tier C).
- Run residency-check and attach snapshot to ticket.
- Apply soft-pin flag; record change-id and notify customer.
- Watch telemetry for 72 hours; if P95 latency > baseline + 200ms escalate.

Governance and retention notes:
- Evidence bundles retained for 90 days by default for Tier B; Tier C retention per contract.
- Audit logs for operator actions maintained for 365 days.

Appendix: sample cost table (example numbers for initial quoting)
- Soft-pin uplift: 10% for low-volume (<50M tokens/month), 15% for medium (50–250M), 20% for >250M.
- Hard-pin fixed surcharge: $2k/mo for <=10GB anchored data, $5k/mo for 10–100GB, $8k+ for >100GB (subject to finance approval).

Quick history and context notes (notes to self):
- Pulled numbers from residency-cost-prototype spreadsheet (link to GH PR above).
- Example customer ask Nov 2024: EU SMB with legal clause asking for residency evidence; soft-pin trial reduced cross-border egress by ~40% but increased P95 by ~80ms.

Action items (owner initials):
- Finance: propose formal SKU table for SMB tiers (Aisha)
- Legal: standard clause for Tier B evidence acceptance (Rachel)
- Infra: dashboard prototype (Diego)
- Product: confirm wording for onboarding flow and UX (Marcus)

Notes to reviewers: This is a working doc -- expect lots of iteration. Feedback welcome inline or via Slack #residency-ops.

Unresolved: exact X threshold where dedicated pricing is cheaper than sustained soft-pin uplift (TBD; need cost model to compute).
